title: MRP-VM
lines: MRP-VM presents an architecture for building and improving custom agent systems under explicit control.
Its central distinction is between a successful answer and a maintained organizational capability.
The book explains how procedures, evidence, permissions, and versions can stay connected.
A proposed improvement must remain separate from the authority that activates it.
Readers can examine that design without mistaking its research ambitions for proven reliability.

title: An answer is not a capability
chapter: An answer is not a capability
lines: A successful response may depend on assumptions that nobody recorded for the next request.
The book proposes maintaining procedures, tests, and interpreters as versioned Agentic Knowledge Units.
Explicit plans connect work with dependencies and qualifications for its results.
This creates a place to preserve how a recurring task should be performed.
The research question is whether that structure produces more repeatable, governable capability.

title: A candidate stays a candidate
lines: Operational feedback can motivate a candidate revision without changing the active procedure immediately.
The proposed process compares candidates against baselines and checks for regressions.
Proposal, evaluation, approval, and activation remain separate responsibilities.
Published versions retain a coherent identity and a target for rollback.
The book uses these distinctions to connect improvement with control over consequential change.

title: Read the maintained practice
lines: Start with the gap between a good answer and a repeatable organizational practice.
Then follow the architecture through explicit work, qualification, trace, and controlled improvement.
The design is a research direction whose claims still require comparative evidence.
It is not presented as a frozen manual for one software release.
Read MRP-VM to evaluate how model capability might become maintained institutional capability.
